title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Rose Hill destinations for studying, gathering, campus rituals, and noticing Fordham’s shared history.

cards.title: Walsh Family Library
cards.subtitle: Rose Hill campus library
cards.notes: Set up for a study session in the library, then check its live hours page before planning an evening visit.
cards.short_summary: A campus library with regular-session late closing on most weekdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham lists Walsh Library at Rose Hill with regular-session hours until midnight Monday through Thursday and Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Regular-session hours shown by Fordham: Mon–Thu and Sun until 12 a.m.; hours may change by semester.

cards.title: LITE Center
cards.subtitle: Walsh Library lower level, Room 014
cards.notes: Use the collaboration areas for a group work block, or plan a project around its makerspace and recording rooms.
cards.short_summary: A technology workspace with collaboration, XR, recording, and making facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham says Rose Hill students have free access to the LITE Center’s collaboration areas, recording rooms, XR space, and makerspace.
cards.access_notes: Fordham locates it in Walsh Library lower level, Room 014; the page lists Monday–Thursday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: McShane Campus Center First Floor
cards.subtitle: McShane Campus Center, Rose Hill
cards.notes: Meet at a communal table for a low-key work session, or take a break in the lounge and pool area.
cards.short_summary: A student-facing floor built around lounging, pool, and communal tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham describes the first floor as a gathering space where students play pool, relax in the lounge, and work at communal tables.
cards.access_notes: Located within the Joseph M. McShane, S.J., Campus Center; check building access before visiting.

cards.title: Campus Center Lawn
cards.subtitle: At McShane Campus Center, Rose Hill
cards.notes: Use the named lawn as a simple outdoor meeting point, then move indoors if weather or campus programming changes.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor destination directly identified on Fordham’s Rose Hill map.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s Rose Hill campus map lists Campus Center Lawn as part of the McShane Campus Center.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; availability can be affected by weather and scheduled events.

cards.title: Edwards Parade
cards.subtitle: Historic quadrangle at Rose Hill
cards.notes: Walk through the quad and read its context before an event; it is also the destination for Fordham’s commencement procession.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus quadrangle tied to University Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham identifies Edwards Parade as a traditional college quadrangle and says the commencement procession moves to its entrance.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus area; respect any event setup, posted boundaries, and University directions.

cards.title: Keating Steps
cards.subtitle: Outside Keating Hall, Rose Hill
cards.notes: Pause at the steps during a campus walk and use the occasion to look toward Edwards Parade and the terrace below.
cards.short_summary: A named Rose Hill landmark used for an official Senior Week class-photo event.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s 2026 Senior Week schedule places the Always a Ram Celebration and Class of 2026 Photo at Keating Steps.
cards.source_title: Senior Week at Rose Hill | Fordham
cards.access_notes: Exterior steps; keep clear during ceremonies, scheduled photography, and active building access.

cards.title: Terrace of the Presidents
cards.subtitle: Between Edwards Parade and Keating Hall
cards.notes: Walk the granite steps slowly and look for the engraved names of honorary-degree recipients rather than treating it as a shortcut.
cards.short_summary: A stair terrace whose engraved stones record visiting heads of state.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham says the granite steps between Edwards Parade and the Keating Hall Terrace carry names of heads of state who received honorary doctorates.
cards.access_notes: Exterior steps on the Rose Hill campus; use normal pedestrian care and honor event access controls.

cards.title: Victory Bell
cards.subtitle: In front of the Rose Hill Gymnasium
cards.notes: Find the bell outside the gym and read the nearby context; save ringing or event participation for authorized University occasions.
cards.short_summary: A historic ship’s bell that marks commencement and Fordham athletic victories.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham states that the Victory Bell stands in front of the Rose Hill gymnasium, begins commencement, and traditionally peals after Ram victories.
cards.access_notes: View from the gym exterior; do not assume public permission to ring or handle the bell.

cards.title: Carolyn Dursi Cunniffe Fountain
cards.subtitle: Near Cunniffe House, Rose Hill
cards.notes: Add the fountain to a walk between Keating and nearby halls, and keep the stop brief if the surrounding paths are busy.
cards.short_summary: A named Rose Hill fountain associated with Cunniffe House.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham identifies the Carolyn Dursi Cunniffe Fountain as one of two Rose Hill campus landmarks named for Maurice and Carolyn Cunniffe.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; observe posted restrictions and do not enter the fountain area.

cards.title: 9/11 Memorial Garden
cards.subtitle: Rose Hill campus memorial garden
cards.notes: Visit quietly as part of a campus walk, allowing space for reflection and for anyone using the memorial area.
cards.short_summary: A named memorial garden marked on Fordham’s Rose Hill campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s Rose Hill campus map identifies the 9/11 Memorial Garden as a named campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Memorial setting on campus; keep the visit respectful and follow any posted guidance.
